sourceSnapshots.title: Enforce data integrity with constraints
sourceSnapshots.shortSummary: The unit distinguishes primary, foreign, unique, CHECK, DEFAULT and NOT NULL constraints, and describes table-independent sequence allocation and range reservation.

sourceSnapshots.title: Unique constraints and check constraints
sourceSnapshots.shortSummary: UNIQUE applies to the specified column tuple and permits NULL under its documented uniqueness rule; CHECK rejects FALSE rather than UNKNOWN and enforces row-level predicates.

sourceSnapshots.title: Sequence numbers
sourceSnapshots.shortSummary: Sequences allocate independently of transactions and tables; unused or rolled-back allocations can leave gaps. Repeated references to the same sequence within one statement share a value per output row.

sourceSnapshots.title: decimal and numeric (Transact-SQL)
sourceSnapshots.shortSummary: DECIMAL precision counts total digits and scale counts fractional digits; integral capacity is p-s. Precision 1–9 uses five bytes, 10–19 nine bytes, and narrowing scale can round values.

sourceSnapshots.title: CREATE COLUMNSTORE INDEX (Transact-SQL)
sourceSnapshots.shortSummary: A nonclustered columnstore can retain rowstore base organization, select supported columns and filter rows. Its SQL Server 2022 syntax differs from clustered conversion and excludes INCLUDE and nvarchar(max) columns.

sourceSnapshots.title: Optimize with indexes
sourceSnapshots.shortSummary: The unit distinguishes base rowstore/clustered columnstore organization from secondary nonclustered columnstore for operational analytics while retaining transactional access paths.

sourceSnapshots.title: Create a system-versioned temporal table
sourceSnapshots.shortSummary: The current creation article requires temporal history to match current-table column count, names, order and types. History cannot have a primary key or unique index. Skipping temporal data consistency checks does not waive those schema requirements.

sourceSnapshots.title: Manage JSON columns and indexes
sourceSnapshots.shortSummary: The unit separates typed relational columns from variable JSON attributes, demonstrates indexed computed scalar projections, and explicitly calls JSON_MODIFY for JSON text updates.

sourceSnapshots.title: JSON data in SQL Server
sourceSnapshots.shortSummary: SQL supports mixed relational and JSON columns and explicit text mutation of array elements. The current overview marks native json and several SQL Server 2025 JSON extensions generally available.

sourceSnapshots.title: Primary and foreign key constraints
sourceSnapshots.shortSummary: Foreign keys enforce referenced-row integrity and distinguish NO ACTION, CASCADE, SET NULL and SET DEFAULT. SET DEFAULT still produces values that must satisfy the foreign key; defaults are not exemptions.

sourceSnapshots.title: ALTER PARTITION FUNCTION (Transact-SQL)
sourceSnapshots.shortSummary: ALTER PARTITION FUNCTION atomically changes every dependent table/index. All using schemes need NEXT USED for a split; merging removes a boundary but preserves and combines rows.

sourceSnapshots.title: Partition tables for scale
sourceSnapshots.shortSummary: Partitioning uses a function for boundaries, a scheme for storage placement and suitable aligned indexes for maintenance. The unit names ALTER PARTITION FUNCTION for splits and merges.

sources.contentRelevance: The current official guide still explicitly measures the March 12, 2026 outline. Its three domains retain weights 35-40%, 35-40% and 25-30%, with 11 skills and 73 subskills. The refreshed extraction has no objective-content change. This establishes scope, not technical correctness or feature availability.

sources.title: Develop AI-enabled database solutions
sources.contentRelevance: The current DP-800T00-A course covers SQL Server, Azure SQL and SQL databases in Fabric. It is an ancestry-only preparation bridge: current credential HTML references its exact course UID, and current course HTML references the three self-paced path UIDs. The overview is not technical evidence for answers.

parents.evidenceSummary: The current official credential HTML contains data-learn-uid="course.dp-800t00" in its Learning Paths preparation container. The separately retrieved canonical course identifies itself as Course DP-800T00-A and links back to this credential.
parents.relevanceJustification: This exact credential-owned preparation reference establishes the current course bridge. Neither the scheduling link nor the course overview is being treated as proof of GA, an objective map, or implementation correctness.

sources.title: Design and develop database solutions
sources.contentRelevance: The current self-paced path links four modules for database objects, programmability, advanced T-SQL and AI-assisted SQL development. It supplies the finite preparation ancestry for the first domain. Exact implementation claims require the linked teaching units and their directly referenced product documentation.

parents.evidenceSummary: The current course HTML explicitly references data-learn-uid="learn.wwl.design-develop-database-solutions". The retrieved path HTML has that exact uid and the canonical English path URL; its MCP content exposes the four linked modules.
parents.relevanceJustification: The exact matching UID and canonical path bind this course reference to the actual self-paced design path, rather than inferring approval from a similar title, hostname or subject.

sources.title: Design and implement database objects with SQL
sources.contentRelevance: DP-800's design path links this module's table, index, specialized-table, constraint, JSON and partitioning units. The module is a navigation ancestor, not implementation proof.

parents.evidenceSummary: The September 16 design-path MCP body links Design and implement database objects with SQL through ../../modules/design-implement-database-objects/.
parents.relevanceJustification: This is the exact object-design module named by the current course-linked path, covering the first DP-800 domain skill.

sources.title: Enforce data integrity with constraints
sources.contentRelevance: The unit distinguishes primary, foreign, unique, CHECK, DEFAULT and NOT NULL constraints, and describes table-independent sequence allocation and range reservation.

parents.evidenceSummary: The fresh object module links Enforce data integrity with constraints at 6-design-implement-constraints.
parents.relevanceJustification: This unit explicitly teaches the constraint and sequence subskills and names the implementation topics needed for preserved records 001–003.

sources.title: Manage JSON columns and indexes
sources.contentRelevance: The unit separates typed relational columns from variable JSON attributes, demonstrates indexed computed scalar projections, and explicitly calls JSON_MODIFY for JSON text updates.

parents.evidenceSummary: The object module directly links Manage JSON columns and indexes at 7-design-implement-json.
parents.relevanceJustification: The unit grounds JSON column/index design and explicitly references the JSON_MODIFY API used by retained advanced SQL questions.

sources.title: Unique constraints and check constraints
sources.contentRelevance: UNIQUE applies to the specified column tuple and permits NULL under its documented uniqueness rule; CHECK rejects FALSE rather than UNKNOWN and enforces row-level predicates.

parents.evidenceSummary: The current constraints unit explicitly references the Unique constraints and check constraints article, including its CHECK and UNIQUE sections. The query-free implementation URL was freshly fetched.
parents.relevanceJustification: This exact product contract resolves tuple uniqueness and UNKNOWN semantics that the two retained constraint scenarios depend on.

sources.title: Sequence numbers
sources.contentRelevance: Sequences allocate independently of transactions and tables; unused or rolled-back allocations can leave gaps. Repeated references to the same sequence within one statement share a value per output row.

parents.evidenceSummary: The constraints unit's sequence section names and references the Sequence numbers product article; its canonical query-free URL was independently fetched in this pass.
parents.relevanceJustification: The exact allocation contract is needed for sequence lifecycle and code traces within the current sequence objective.

sources.title: Build effective tables
sources.contentRelevance: Table design balances exact numeric types, bounded columns, integrity and workload-specific indexing; the unit explicitly discusses DECIMAL precision and storage.

parents.evidenceSummary: The current objects module links Build effective tables at 3-design-implement-tables.
parents.relevanceJustification: This exact table-design unit is the ancestry for data-type sizing decisions within the first object subskill.

sources.title: Optimize with indexes
sources.contentRelevance: The unit distinguishes base rowstore/clustered columnstore organization from secondary nonclustered columnstore for operational analytics while retaining transactional access paths.

parents.evidenceSummary: The fresh objects module links Optimize with indexes at 4-design-implement-indexes.
parents.relevanceJustification: The linked unit directly introduces the two columnstore forms and supports the exact statement-reference approval proposal.

sources.title: Use specialized table types
sources.contentRelevance: Specialized table choices include memory-optimized, temporal, external, ledger and graph tables, with links to their dedicated creation and architecture contracts.

parents.evidenceSummary: The object module directly links Use specialized table types at 5-specialized-table-types.
parents.relevanceJustification: This is the current credential-linked preparation unit for specialized tables and the immediate source of the proposed exact product references.

sources.title: Partition tables for scale
sources.contentRelevance: Partitioning uses a function for boundaries, a scheme for storage placement and suitable aligned indexes for maintenance. The unit names ALTER PARTITION FUNCTION for splits and merges.

parents.evidenceSummary: The current objects module directly links Partition tables for scale at 8-design-implement-partitioning.
parents.relevanceJustification: This unit provides genuine ancestry for partition layout and lifecycle implementation decisions.

sources.title: JSON data in SQL Server
sources.contentRelevance: SQL supports mixed relational and JSON columns and explicit text mutation of array elements. The current overview marks native json and several SQL Server 2025 JSON extensions generally available.

parents.evidenceSummary: The JSON columns unit explicitly references JSON data in SQL Server via its JSON columns link. The exact query-free overview was freshly fetched.
parents.relevanceJustification: This direct training reference supplies the current hybrid-column overview and indexed-array mutation example, not a doc-to-doc approval.

sources.title: decimal and numeric (Transact-SQL)
sources.contentRelevance: DECIMAL precision counts total digits and scale counts fractional digits; integral capacity is p-s. Precision 1–9 uses five bytes, 10–19 nine bytes, and narrowing scale can round values.

parents.evidenceSummary: Build effective tables explicitly names DECIMAL(10,2), precision-sensitive financial values and storage sizing. The precise decimal-and-numeric type reference was freshly fetched.
parents.relevanceJustification: The named data type's exact p/s and storage contract is necessary to validate the table sizing subskill; topical float assumptions are not substituted.

sources.title: CREATE COLUMNSTORE INDEX (Transact-SQL)
sources.contentRelevance: A nonclustered columnstore can retain rowstore base organization, select supported columns and filter rows. Its SQL Server 2022 syntax differs from clustered conversion and excludes INCLUDE and nvarchar(max) columns.

parents.evidenceSummary: Optimize with indexes explicitly names and demonstrates CREATE NONCLUSTERED COLUMNSTORE INDEX and its clustered counterpart. The corresponding statement article was fetched directly.
parents.relevanceJustification: The exact statement contract supplies the supported filtered form and data-type limitations needed to compare realistic operational-analytics designs.

sources.title: Create a system-versioned temporal table
sources.contentRelevance: The current creation article requires temporal history to match current-table column count, names, order and types. History cannot have a primary key or unique index. Skipping temporal data consistency checks does not waive those schema requirements.

parents.evidenceSummary: The frozen specialized-table training unit explicitly links the former creation article. New HTTP GET receipts show that both the legacy citation and the actual azure-portal training link redirect to the /tables/temporal/create article; the final sql-server-ver17 selector is a same-document presentation view. The query-free canonical article was independently retrieved through Microsoft Learn MCP.
parents.relevanceJustification: The canonical article is the observed redirect successor of the exact creation reference in credential-linked training. Its current-table/history schema rules and user-defined-history restrictions directly support the existing specialized-table candidate, without a doc-to-doc provenance chain.

sources.title: Primary and foreign key constraints
sources.contentRelevance: Foreign keys enforce referenced-row integrity and distinguish NO ACTION, CASCADE, SET NULL and SET DEFAULT. SET DEFAULT still produces values that must satisfy the foreign key; defaults are not exemptions.

parents.evidenceSummary: The constraints training unit explicitly references primary/foreign-key constraints and their cascading referential actions. This precise article was freshly fetched.
parents.relevanceJustification: The direct training reference establishes delete-action alternatives and their integrity requirements for the constraint subskill.

sources.title: ALTER PARTITION FUNCTION (Transact-SQL)
sources.contentRelevance: ALTER PARTITION FUNCTION atomically changes every dependent table/index. All using schemes need NEXT USED for a split; merging removes a boundary but preserves and combines rows.

parents.evidenceSummary: Partition tables for scale explicitly links ALTER PARTITION FUNCTION for split/merge maintenance. The exact implementation article was freshly fetched.
parents.relevanceJustification: This named statement contract supports source-specific maintenance diagnostics and corrects the unit's misleading archive-by-merge description.

evidenceCautions: Constraint training overstates enforcement across all ingestion paths. The retained candidate uses an enabled CHECK and future ordinary inserts; no bypass-proof assertion is approved.

The table ancestor mislabels DECIMAL(10,2) as five bytes and oversimplifies character width. Only the exact DECIMAL product contract supports d1-001; no held external-string or computed-key guarantee is approved.
The index training overview simplifies delta-rowgroup thresholds and uses broad performance language. d1-002 uses exact NCCI eligibility and explicitly disclaims guaranteed performance.
The temporal source is the new canonical MCP body with fresh actual dates, not the prior citation. History constraints are not current-table constraints, and OFF does not waive schema validation.

The JSON unit labels a 2025 modify method Preview while the overview describes newer GA enhancements. d1-007 uses established 2022 textual JSON; neither the source Not applicable label nor later GA list establishes a new 2022 feature.
The partition unit calls bare MERGE archival. The exact function article says it retains values in a remaining partition; d1-011 deliberately requires a separately validated archive switch-out.

relatedConceptDecisions.reasoningDifference: The first asks which values an enabled nullable CHECK admits, the second which rows compare equal as a business key, and held d1-008 how a referential delete substitutes a fallback owner. Each needs a different engine contract, not renamed entities.

Removing ROLLBACK changes the first item’s challenge but does not affect the second. Conversely, replacing the paired SELECT with separate allocation statements changes d1-009 while leaving transaction-independent consumption in direct-003 unchanged.

Held d1-006 concerns a computed scalar’s admissible key width and truncation contract. d1-007 concerns whether required relational fields are stored outside a variable document and whether new categories need DDL. A hybrid schema does not answer the key-width problem.

A destination-ready function can still fail the archive goal in d1-011 because MERGE retains rows. A successful switch-out does not assign another scheme’s NEXT USED in d1-010. The questions test different state transitions and failure causes.
NCCI versus rowstore/LOB/row-filter eligibility is independent of CCI partition occupancy and archive placement. Recognizing the word columnstore alone cannot solve either complete scenario.

Exact decimal integral/fractional capacity and its declared byte tier do not establish an external text encoding/length contract. The held external-table question is not approved by analogy with numeric sizing.

duplicateAndQualityInspection.warningResolution: Each affected question has its own answerClues, stemSufficiency and qualityReviewed analysis above/in validation-metadata. Negative rules constrain real requirements; pronouns refer to named statements/tables; the NCCI absolute is a bounded preservation rule. Difficulty, familiar setups and weaker distractors receive individual score deductions.
duplicateAndQualityInspection.limitations: Prior cross-exam results were read, not rerun as an exhaustive semantic review. Deterministic checks do not establish worldwide originality. Held related candidates were compared for reasoning only, not technically or adversarially approved.
